Definition: in a good sense, trust; in a bad one, silliness
BiblicalUsage: Kislah holds two meanings at once: in a good sense, trust; in a bad one, silliness. Job 4:6 asks, is not this thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways, while Psalms 85:8 warns God's saints not to turn again to folly.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the one word carries its own warning: confidence in God and folly look alike from the outside, and only the direction of the trust tells them apart.
